newsitem.title: INDIA: India house approves bill on depository trade.
newsitem.headline: India house approves bill on depository trade.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament on Wednesday approved a bill to allow the securities of state-run banks and financial institutions to be traded through share depositories, the United News of India (UNI) said.

Earlier, a technical stipulation did not allow securities of the Industrial Development Bank of India, the Unit Trust of India, the State Bank of India and other state-run banks to be traded on the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL).
Depositories allow the registration and transfer of shares by electronic means.

The bill was moved in Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, for approval of an ordinance issued by a presidential decree in January to make the changes to allow the securities to be traded through the NSDL.
The upper house, Rajya Sabha, must also approve the bill before it becomes law. Approval by the upper house is expected to be a formality.
